note: The offline demonstration transcript for the Node.js pipeline demo. It drives the real tool registry and the real agent loop: inspect, propose, get approval, measure the estimator error, fix the divisor in the workspace, measure again, run the project tests, keep the follow-up in the backlog, and close.

arguments.objective: find out why the variance is wrong, fix the estimator, and check the fix

gaps.title: the variance is the population estimator, not the sample one
gaps.why: the README documents sample variance (n - 1) but the code divides by n
gaps.condition: no test compares the variance with the known sample variance

tasks.title: measure the estimator error
tasks.question: how far is the variance from the exact sample variance?

tasks.title: fix the divisor and re-measure
tasks.question: does the error vanish with n - 1?
tasks.method: change the pipeline in the workspace, run the experiment and the tests
tasks.success_criteria: variance_error is 0 and the tests pass

arguments.success_criteria: the estimator is explained, fixed in the workspace, and the new numbers are measured

arguments.text: variance_error is -0.5714285714285712: the estimator divides by n, not n - 1
arguments.uncertainty: the divisor is the suspected cause, not yet verified

arguments.text: after the fix variance_error is 0 and mean_error stays 0
arguments.uncertainty: only this dataset of eight measurements has been checked

arguments.title: estimator bias across sample sizes
arguments.question: how does the population-versus-sample variance gap shrink as n grows?
arguments.reason: the fix changes the estimator for every dataset, and only n = 8 is measured
arguments.methodology: sweep dataset sizes and compare both estimators with the exact sample variance
arguments.success_criteria: the gap is characterised across sizes

arguments.summary: the pipeline used the population variance estimator while the project documents the sample one; the workspace copy now divides by n - 1, the measured error is zero, and the project tests pass
